consensus_summary: Works are human deeds/actions that outwardly express and evidence the inner spiritual condition: good works as the visible fruit of genuine faith, grace, and regeneration; evil works as the fruit of unbelief, the flesh, or darkness. They function as evidence/fruit (not the root of salvation) and form the basis of divine judgment, though traditions differ on their exact soteriological role.
book_summary: Works are simply deeds, not a synonym for obedience. A work becomes obedience only when it executes a legitimate command (or disobedience when it conflicts with God's command). Romans 4 treats the laborer's work as offered for wages/debt; James 2 treats Abraham's work as faith made visible. Even complete obedience earns no wage, since the servant has only done his duty.
consensus_core_identification: human deeds/actions that manifest inner spiritual state (good as fruit of faith/grace; evil as fruit of unbelief/flesh)
book_core_identification: deeds (explicitly not synonymous with obedience); a work becomes obedience only by executing a legitimate command, and complete obedience remains mere duty that earns no wage
boundary_disagreement: Book sharply separates works/deeds from obedience (conditioning the latter on execution of a legitimate command) and insists complete obedience still earns nothing; consensus routinely presents good works as acts of obedience/love/mercy without this separation and often treats 'works' in Pauline texts as including human obedience/effort set against faith.
material_contradiction: None; both identify the referent as deeds, and the book retains the evidential use in James and the wage contrast in Romans without denying the fruit/evidence role.
rationale: Minimum cores both reduce to 'deeds/actions.' The book preserves that general category and the Rom 4 / Jas 2 usages while materially tightening boundaries and conditions: it rejects synonymy with obedience, reclassifies when a deed counts as obedience vs. mere work, and foregrounds the Luke 17 duty/no-wage principle. This is refinement of extension and precision, not replacement of the central referent or a novel category outside the consensus.
strongest_objection: Consensus already defines works primarily as deeds rather than as a strict synonym for obedience, so the book's distinction may be only a minor clarifying nuance rather than a material change of boundary.
